questions.stem: What is the correct sequence in closed-loop communication?
options: Order given, repeated back, then confirmed or corrected
The order is given and the receiver carries it out in silence
The order is written down first and then given out loud
The receiver confirms before the order has been given
questions.explanation: Closed loop is give, repeat back, confirm. Carrying out an order silently leaves errors uncaught.

questions.stem: You cannot hear an order over engine noise. What should you do?
options: Guess what was most likely said and act on it
Wait to see what the other crew members do
Ignore it until it is repeated by someone else
Ask the officer to repeat it before acting
questions.explanation: The correct step is to ask for clarification before acting. Guessing or waiting risks a wrong action.

questions.stem: A rating reports "Something over there" to the officer. What is wrong with this as a report?
options: It should have been given straight to the master
It should have been passed by radio, not by voice
It is vague and gives no bearing or proper terms
Nothing is wrong; short reports are always best
questions.explanation: Reports use correct shipboard terms and specific bearings such as "starboard bow". "Over there" cannot be acted on. Reports go to the officer of the watch.

questions.stem: Where does the Navigation Safety Regulations say the working language for navigational safety must be recorded?
options: It is not recorded anywhere on board
In the official log book (or any log book)
On the chart in use, near the title
In the radio log only, at each watch change
questions.explanation: The master or authorized representative determines the working language and records it in the official log book, or any log book where the Division does not apply.

questions.stem: Which statement matches s. 137 on what crew members must be able to do in the working language?
options: Understand it, and give orders and report back in it as needed
Only read it, so that written notices can be followed
Only speak it in an emergency, when the alarm has sounded
Understand it only if they hold an officer's certificate
questions.explanation: Each crew member must be able to understand the working language, give orders and instructions in it if appropriate, and report back in it if appropriate.

questions.stem: Which set of communications must be in English unless everyone directly involved speaks a common language other than English?
options: Engine room orders, galley orders and all deck work orders
Only written logbook entries and the official log
Only distress calls sent to the Coast Guard on channel 16
Bridge-to-bridge, bridge-to-shore, and pilot-to-bridge
questions.explanation: Section 137(3) names bridge-to-bridge and bridge-to-shore safety communications and pilot-to-bridge watchkeeper communications. Other on-board talk uses the working language recorded in the log book.

questions.stem: What must a vessel with an emergency steering position be fitted with?
options: A public address system with one-way speakers
A portable loud hailer kept on the bridge wing
Two-way voice that can pass heading information
A second magnetic compass only, with no other link
questions.explanation: Section 108 requires a two-way voice link able to communicate heading information to the emergency steering position.

questions.stem: Which pair of VHF channels is correct?
options: Channel 6 for distress, urgency and calling; channel 22 for bridge-to-bridge
16 for distress, safety and calling; 13 for bridge-to-bridge
Channel 13 for distress and calling; channel 16 for bridge-to-bridge
Channel 70 for voice calling; channel 16 for DSC alerts only
questions.explanation: Channel 16 is the voice channel for distress, urgency, safety and calling, and channel 13 is the bridge-to-bridge channel. Channel 70 is for DSC alerts.

questions.stem: A rating notices the ship's general alarm panel has a light they do not recognise. According to the course standard, which skill applies?
options: Know the alarm and comms systems, and ask if unsure
Ignore the panel, because it is only for the engineers
Switch the light off to avoid causing a false alarm
Wait for the next watch and let them sort it out
questions.explanation: TP 10936 expects a rating to be able to use the internal communication and alarm systems. If a light is unfamiliar, ask the officer.

questions.stem: Which description best fits bridge resource management?
options: Giving the master all of the work so nothing is missed
Relying on electronic aids alone
Keeping quiet on the bridge unless the officer asks
Clear roles and good use of all resources
questions.explanation: Bridge resource management is using people, equipment and information effectively, with clear roles. The other options describe poor practice.
